chunks: And Ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Ismāʿīl ibn Sālim, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
A man asked him and said: “May Allah rectify you, is drinking wine worse, or abandoning salat (prayer)?”
Then he said: “Do you know why that is?”
He said: “Because he comes into a state in which he does not recognize his Lord, Mighty and Majestic.”

key_terms.تَرْكُ ٱلصَّلَاةِ: abandoning salat (prayer); a grave sin compared in the question
key_terms.رَبَّهُ: his Lord; Allah as the object of recognition and consciousness
key_terms.شَرٌّ: worse; more evil or harmful in this moral comparison
key_terms.شُرْبُ ٱلْخَمْرِ: drinking intoxicating wine; the sinful act being judged in the narration
key_terms.عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ: Mighty and Majestic; honorific describing Allah
key_terms.لَا يَعْرِفُ: he does not recognize; meaning loss of awareness or recognition
key_terms.يَصِيرُ فِي حَالٍ: he enters a state; indicating a condition caused by intoxication

ai.seo_question: Why does the Imam عليه السلام say drinking alcohol is worse than abandoning prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that drinking khamr is worse than abandoning salat (prayer) because intoxication brings a person into a state of losing awareness of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. It highlights not only the legal prohibition of khamr but also its destructive spiritual effect on recognition of one’s Lord.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4948 - Ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Isma'il ibn Salim, who reported from Abu Abdillah (as) that a man asked him:
"May Allah (swt) rectify you, is drinking alcohol worse or abandoning prayer?"
Then Imam (as) said: "Do you know why that is?"
Imam (as) said: "Because it leads a person to a state where he no longer recognizes his Lord (azj), the Mighty and Majestic."
